faq.a: Mostly by breathing in droplets from an infected dog's coughing, sneezing or barking, or through contact with saliva, urine or feces. Wildlife such as raccoons, skunks and foxes can also carry the virus.

faq.q: What are the first signs of distemper in dogs?
faq.a: Eye discharge is often the first sign, followed by fever, a runny nose, lethargy and poor appetite. Coughing, vomiting, diarrhea and, in some dogs, twitching or seizures can follow.
Some do, and some infections are mild. But no drug kills the virus, the AVMA describes distemper as often fatal, and survivors can have permanent nerve damage, so vaccination is the real protection.
No. Canine distemper does not infect people. It can affect many wild animals, including raccoons, skunks, foxes and ferrets.

faq.q: Can a vaccinated dog get distemper?
faq.a: It is uncommon in dogs that completed the puppy series and boosters. The highest risk is in puppies that haven't finished their shots and in unvaccinated dogs.
